newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Virgin Express to double fleet by year 2000.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Express to double fleet by year 2000.

text.p: British entrepreneur Richard Branson said on Tuesday he expected his cut-price regional airline Virgin Express to more than double the number of its planes by the turn of the century.
"By the turn of the century I would say at least double," Branson told Reuters after a news conference to promote the launch of Virgin Express's Brussels-Copenhagen link.
Brussels-based Virgin Express, launched in April after Branson bought 90 percent of EuroBelgian Airlines SA (EBA), currently operates 14 Boeing 737 planes.
Virgin Express takes delivery of two new Boeing 737-400s early next year but these will replace two existing planes.
Branson said it was not yet clear whether Virgin Express would stick to Boeing planes. "It could also be mixed," he said.
But he noted Virgin was happy with the 737s, calling them lovely planes. "As long as Boeing is willing to sell them to us at a reasonable price we'll carry on buying them," he said.
